input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The single-file wrap now checks isinstance(filename, os.PathLike), so a plain str is no longer wrapped in a tuple and is passed directly to edit_files as an iterable.
- rationale: Trigger: calling click.edit(filename='notes.txt') with a str. The check at line 906 is False for a str, so filename stays a str. edit_files then iterates the string character by character, opening 'n', 'o', 't', and so on as separate files. Impact: the str form of the API, which is the documented common case, opens the wrong files or errors instead of editing notes.txt.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: the isinstance check covers only os.PathLike, so a str is not wrapped in a tuple and edit_files iterates it character by character. It gives the same trigger, click.edit(filename='notes.txt'), and the same outcome of opening single-character files.
